measurements.baseline: declared 12 pt but elements run on a 6 pt half step; item_name y mod 12 pt shows two phases (4.0 and 1.9 mm)

item_pitch_pt_by_card.El Barril: 54 with one-line descriptions (24 pt padding per gap)

measurements.padding_to_fill_rows: El Barril +24 pt per item gap, La Botella +6 pt
measurements.contrast: dark ink and card colours on cream pass 4.5:1; cream-on-rust, cream-on-magenta and cream-on-green bands pass; La Botella band switches to dark ink on marigold

top_problem: The lotería tabla locks the card edges, but not the rows inside the cards: row 1 splits after the second item, row 2 never lines up (La Rosa's first subhead sits opposite 'Straight pours'), and El Barril is padded with 24 pt of dead air per item to reach its frame, so the grid is a frame fitted around uneven lists instead of a system; the boldest missing idea is to make each drink its own small lotería card (numbered, with a figure) laid out as a true tabla grid, so the structure is the menu and not a trim around it.
fixes: Give every card one shared 12 pt row grid, with the item pitch set once for the menu (for example 3 rows per item), so items in facing cards sit on the same baselines and El Barril loses its 24 pt padding.
Put the La Botella 'Straight pours.' note inside the name band or under the first subhead, so both bottom-row cards start their first subhead at 618.7 pt.
Fill the empty space in El Barril and La Botella with real content (style/ABV lines for beer, age or type for spirits) rather than leading, so all four cards have the same density.
Use one name-band ink rule: either cream text on every band (darken the marigold) or dark text everywhere, so the header level has one style.
Snap the header gloss ('Cocktails', 'Beer & Cider') to the name-band caps baseline at one fixed offset from the name, and declare baseline_pt as 6 to match what the layout actually uses.

top_problem: The lotería header system is a strong idea: all four card-name bands share y (74.35 and 205.58 mm, h 7.67 mm), and subheads sit at one x per column (17.46 / 114.83 mm) on the 6 pt grid. The spacing under the headers is not one system, though. Band-to-first-subhead is 12.70 mm on Cantarito, Barril and Rosa but 21.17 mm on La Botella, because the 'Straight pours.' note sits between them. El Barril pads each item gap by 24 pt (~48 mm item pitch against ~24 to 28 mm elsewhere) and La Botella by 6 pt, only to make the columns end together. That leaves visible holes and makes the SIDRA subhead float. The boldest idea still missing: make each card a working lotería card, with the list set inside the card's own frame as the tabla (a bean-marker price token, and the item rows as the card's playing field), rather than a lotería face sitting on top of an ordinary list.
fixes: Give every card the same fixed band-to-first-subhead gap (12 pt) and move La Botella's 'Straight pours.' into the name band as its italic tag (or below the first subhead), so its AGAVE subhead lands at the same offset as CLÁSICOS, DE BARRIL and POR COPA.

Drop the 24 pt and 6 pt padding on El Barril and La Botella; use one item gap on every card and take up the spare height with a card-specific footer (e.g. the 'Ask for today's tap' line or a small cut-paper ornament), so the gaps stop being visibly stretched.

Set La Botella's prices in the card accent colour like the other three cards (they are currently ink), and give each spirit a one-line description so the card has the same item/description/serve rhythm and header-to-item density as the others.

Put the English tag on the name band ('Cocktails', 'Beer & Cider', 'Wine', 'Spirits') at one fixed distance from the Spanish name and on its baseline on every card, and match the subhead English gloss to it, so the two English levels read as one system.
Pull the masthead into the lotería system (a title card or a tabla header with a 'Lotería de la Cantina' line) so the top-level header outranks the card names by concept, not just by size.

lens: palette, contrast, price and number styling

measurements.palette: 4 hues (terracotta #A63C1A, agave #2F5D50, rosa #C2185B, marigold #E3A018) plus cream/ink neutrals: deliberate and on-venue
measurements.price_style: Fraunces 700 11.5 pt, tnum+lnum, whole-dollar numbers with no $ on every card, colour-keyed per card; lotería numerals 11 pt italic ink, so they stay clearly different from prices

top_problem: The palette and prices are correct but safe. Lotería colour-blocking is the default look for Mexican restaurants, and the colour system breaks at La Botella: marigold is too light to use as text, so its prices fall back to plain ink and the one-colour-per-card price idea stops on the fourth card. The boldest idea it's missing is a single owned signature colour moment, such as a saturated rosa or terracotta flood on one hero card or a colour-drenched cover band, instead of four equal pale tints on a washed-out cream.
fixes: Give La Botella a price colour that keeps the per-card system, for example a deep ochre or burnt marigold of about #8A5A00 (check it is at least 4.5:1 on #FBF5EA), instead of falling back to plain ink.
Push one card, ideally El Cantarito, the high-margin cocktails, to a saturated full-colour face or body flood so the palette has a focal point instead of four equally pale tints.
Separate the El Cantarito jug from its face: the terracotta figure on a terracotta tint reads muddy, so tint that face marigold or cream, or give the jug an ink or marigold outline.

Close El Barril's 24 pt padded item gaps, which leave coloured prices floating in empty cream, by adding the beer style and ABV lines or reflowing the rows so the price rhythm matches the other cards.
Raise rosa-on-featured-tint from 4.66:1 to 5:1 or more by darkening rosa text slightly (for example to #A8124D) so the thinnest pair isn't borderline at 8 pt print size.

lens: design concept and elevating elements vs the best bar menus in the country

measurements.price_colour_consistency: card colour on 3 cards, ink on La Botella (inconsistent)

top_problem: The Lotería tabla is the right cultural idea, but it has become the default concept for Mexican restaurants in the US. Here it is used as four framed boxes with clip-art icons and papel picado trim, and the list inside each card is a generic template. The boldest missing idea is to make the menu itself a playable tabla: full-bleed, illustrated card faces that carry the drinks, with the cantor verses rewritten about the actual drinks, a real bean or frijol marker motif, and one hero card for the Margarita, so it becomes an ownable Iowa City cantina artefact and not a themed list.
fixes: Remove the padded 24 pt item gaps in El Barril, which leave visible dead air between the beers; balance the rows by resizing the cards or moving content (for example, give cider a stronger feature) instead of stretching the leading.

Give the concept a hero: make El Cantarito a larger feature card (spanning more height, a richer illustration, the Margarita called out as the house pour with a bean-marker ornament), so the flow is no longer four equal boxes with nothing leading the eye.

Upgrade the flat clip-art figures to one commissioned-looking system, such as cut-paper or woodcut-style illustrations with a consistent line weight and texture, and let each figure fill its face panel the way real lotería art fills its card.
Unify the price styling: La Botella's ink-black prices break the card-colour price system on the other three cards, so either colour every price in its card colour or make every price ink.

Rewrite the verses as drink-specific cantor lines and add a small tabla or marker device (for example 'Lotería' call-out numerals or beans beside featured items), so the lotería concept works as a way to navigate the menu and not only as decoration.

top_problem: The lotería idea stops at a framed card header. On the phone the tabla collapses into four stacked coloured boxes with a chip row, and in print El Barril's 30 pt item gaps (against 6 pt on El Cantarito and 12 pt on La Botella) leave visible holes that give away the fill-the-row trick. The boldest missing idea: make the menu actually play as a lotería. The phone chip row should be a mini tabla of the four figures that deals the cards, and each card face should carry its figure large and edge to edge as a real card does, not as a 69 pt icon beside a verse.
fixes: Stop stretching El Barril to fill its row (item gaps of 30 pt vs 6 pt elsewhere, a spacing inconsistency across cards). Use one item gap on every card and absorb the height difference with a real element: beer-style notes with ABV, a flight line or a larger face figure.

On the phone, the italic numbers 44 / 9 / 41 / 8 in the chips and card corners are larger (24 px) than the prices and compete with them in a menu full of numerals. Cut them to at most the size of the item name, or give them the traditional boxed lotería numeral treatment so they read as card numbers, not prices.

The phone card faces keep the 72 px figure beside a centred verse, so each face reads as an icon plus a caption. On the phone, stack the figure full width above the verse, as on a real lotería card, so the phone version has the print tabla's visual weight.

Beer and wine descriptions ('Dry red wine.', 'Crisp pale lager.') are one flat line while the cocktails get three lines, so on the phone the lower three cards look unfinished. Bring every non-cocktail item to at least a style/region/ABV line so card density matches.

The phone papel picado shows 5 flags and the print shows 11, and the phone has no closing element after La Botella. Scale the banner rhythm to the same flag width and end the phone scroll with a matching papel picado or cantor sign-off so both formats open and close the same way.

lens: every item and price vs build/draft_doc.json; descriptions from known facts; section order for a Mexican restaurant and cocktail bar in Iowa City
top_problem: Content is uneven across categories. Cocktails get full spirit, modifier, garnish and serve lines. Beer, cider and wine print only the draft's generic one-liners ('Dry red wine.', 'Crisp pale lager.'). The three spirits print no description at all. At a Mexican cantina, agave sits in the least-read corner (bottom right) while beer, with only three items and 30 pt gaps, takes the prime top-right card.
problems: Items and prices: all 14 draft items are present. Nothing is invented or dropped, and every price matches the draft exactly (Margarita 15, Manhattan 15, Brown Butter Old Fashioned 16, House Daiquiri 14, Blanco Tequila 12, Añejo Tequila 16, Cognac VSOP 18, Czech Pilsner 7, Dry-Hopped IPA 8, Amber Lager 7, Dry Cider 8, Malbec 12, Pinot Grigio 11, Brut Rosé 13).

Blanco Tequila, Añejo Tequila and Cognac VSOP print name and price only. The single card note 'Straight pours.' is not an item description, so 3 of 14 items fail the rule that every item has a description.

Wine prints no region for any wine. Pinot Grigio and Malbec show only 'Dry white/red wine.', and Brut Rosé shows no grape or region. Beer and cider show no ABV. All of these are correctly flagged in missing_ingredients, but the printed lines stay thin and generic.
Brut Rosé's price label is empty in the draft, so the guest cannot tell whether 13 is a glass or a bottle. It is printed under 'Espumoso · Sparkling' with no pour label.

Price colour changes between cards: terracotta, agave green and rosa on three cards, ink on La Botella. The format is the same everywhere (whole numbers, no $), but the price styling is not one system.
Layout and flow: El Barril spreads 4 items over a 360 pt card with 30 pt gaps and looks hollow, while agave, the house's signature category, is pushed to the bottom-right card.
Coherence: cocktails carry a separate italic serve line, but no other category has an equivalent. The copy depth changes from rich to one-liner to nothing from card to card.
fixes: Give each spirit its own one-line description built only from known facts (e.g. 'Unaged 100% agave' is not allowed unless sourced; at minimum the draft class: 'Blanco / plata tequila, served neat' and 'VSOP cognac, served neat'), and get brand, age statement and pour size from the venue before print.
Label the Brut Rosé price as glass or bottle once the venue confirms it, and add a 'Glass' pour label under 'Por Copa' so the wine prices are unambiguous.

Get region for all three wines and ABV plus brewery for the three beers and the cider from the venue, and print them in one consistent format (e.g. 'Pinot Grigio · Veneto, Italy' / 'Czech Pilsner · 4.8% ABV').
Move La Botella (agave) into the top-right prime card and combine beer and cider into a denser lower card, instead of padding El Barril with 30 pt item gaps.
Print every price in one colour (ink, or each card's accent applied the same way on all four cards) so the price column reads as one system across the tabla.

lens: ingredient names and description completeness (vs build/draft_doc.json)
top_problem: Every item and price matches the draft (13 of 13, none invented, changed or dropped). But the three spirits (Blanco Tequila 12, Añejo Tequila 16, Cognac VSOP 18) have empty descriptions with only a card-level 'Straight pours.', and the wine and beer lines are still thin draft stubs ('Dry red wine.', 'Crisp pale lager.') with no grape or region and no style/ABV. Only the four cocktails meet criterion 8. The gaps are correctly flagged in missing_ingredients, which is why this is not an automatic fail, but half the menu is unfinished in the one venue where agave should be the hero.
fixes: Give each spirit a one-line description from known facts only (for example 'Unaged 100% agave tequila' is not in the draft, so use 'Blanco tequila, served neat' / 'Añejo tequila, served neat' / 'VSOP Cognac, served neat' from the draft names and the 'Straight pours by category' section note), and keep brand, age and pour flagged, so no item prints a name and price alone.

Fill the wine and beer lines with the facts the draft already holds (Malbec and Pinot Grigio are grape names, so print them as 'Malbec · dry red, by the glass' and 'Pinot Grigio · dry white, by the glass'; print 'Pilsner-style lager, draft', 'IPA, draft' and 'Amber lager, draft'), and leave clearly styled 'ABV / region to come' placeholders only if the venue answers the needs_input questions before print.

Put the sections in the same order in doc.json and the phone render as on the letter page (the doc currently runs Cocktails → Spirits → Beer → Cider → Wine while the letter reads Cocktails → Beer & Cider → Wine → Spirits), so one order holds on paper and on the phone.

Remove the large empty gaps between the three beer rows in El Barril, which are stretched to match the cocktail row heights; let short beer and wine rows sit at their natural spacing, or use that space for the ABV/style line once supplied.

Make the La Botella spirits prices the same accent colour as the other three cards' prices (they are currently black while every other card uses its accent), so price styling is one system across the menu.

lens: flow and section order for a Mexican restaurant and cocktail bar in Iowa City
top_problem: For a Mexican cantina, agave is the signature category, but it sits in the weakest slot on the page (bottom right, last in reading order). Its card also reads worst: three bare name-and-price lines under 'Straight pours.' And the Beer card only matches its row height because the item gaps were stretched to 30 pt, against 6 pt on the Cocktails and Wine cards, so the Beer list looks thin. The two strongest things this venue sells (Margarita then tequila) are split between opposite corners, and the order reads like any generic bar: cocktails, beer, wine, spirits.
fixes: Move La Botella (agave) next to El Cantarito in the top row, or stack it directly under the cocktails in column 1, so Margarita then tequila forms one agave path in the prime spots; put Beer and Wine in the second row and balance heights by re-proportioning the faces rather than stretching item gaps.
Make item-to-item spacing the same on all four cards (one value, e.g. 6 or 12 pt) and absorb row-height differences in the face or name band, so El Barril stops reading as 30 pt holes between beers.

Print the missing_ingredients questions as a visible TBC checklist for the venue (beer brewery and ABV, wine region, tequila and cognac brand, age and pour); until they are answered, criterion 8 stays capped because Malbec 'Dry red wine.' and three description-less spirits do not meet the grape + region / type + age standard.
Give prices one colour treatment across all cards (La Botella's prices are ink while the other three use the card colour), and label the Brut Rosé price once the venue confirms glass or bottle.

Reconsider the drunkenness-themed cantor verses on El Barril ('quedó como barril') and La Botella ('La herramienta del borracho') for a university-town menu; keep the lotería device but check the tone with the venue so it doesn't read as promoting heavy drinking.

top_problem: The copy speaks in three different voices. The cocktails get rich, sourced descriptions with serve cues. Beer and wine get one-line taxonomy stubs that restate the name ('Dry red wine.', 'Hop-forward draft IPA.', 'Crisp pale lager.'). The three spirits print a name and price only. So in a Mexican cantina the agave card is the thinnest and has the least copy, and two of the four cantor verses celebrate drunkenness ('Tanto bebió el albañil, que quedó como barril'; 'La herramienta del borracho') in a college-town bar. That tone does not match the rest of the menu. All 14 prices match build/draft_doc.json exactly (no items were invented or dropped; Dry Cider was moved under El Barril). Missing brand, ABV, region and pour facts are flagged, not invented.
fixes: Bring beer, wine and spirits up to the cocktail voice using only known facts plus visible placeholders from missing_ingredients: beer shows style and ABV, wine shows grape and region, spirits show type and age (for example Añejo shows its aging once it is supplied). Stop restating the item name, and push the ask for ABV, region, brand and age as a blocking input before print.

Replace the two drinking-to-excess verses (El Barril, La Botella) with traditional lotería verses or dichos that do not joke about drunkenness, or add a small English gloss under each verse so non-Spanish readers get the same voice. Right now the subheads are bilingual and the verses are not.

Make the subhead pattern the same everywhere as SPANISH · English. 'AGAVE · Tequila' and 'BRANDY · Cognac' break the Clásicos/De Barril/Por Copa pattern; use 'TEQUILA · Agave' / 'COÑAC · Cognac' or the like, and give every card the same card-level line (only La Botella has 'Straight pours.').

Fix the flow: El Barril's 30 pt item gaps read as padding next to 6 pt gaps elsewhere, and agave spirits sit last and smallest in a Mexican cantina. Give tequila more emphasis (for example cross-reference the blanco in the Margarita, or add a 'pour / flight' serve line once the pour size is known) instead of spreading beer items to fill the row.

Label the pour on every price that needs one (spirits pour size, the Brut Rosé glass or bottle) once supplied, so the single right-aligned integer price column carries the same meaning in all four cards.

lens: how missing data is handled and flagged (vs build/draft_doc.json)
top_problem: One change to the source data is not flagged. In the draft, Manhattan has meta.public_components {"aromatic-bitters": false}, which means the bitters should not be shown to guests. round-14/doc.json quietly empties that to {} and prints 'aromatic bitters' in the Manhattan description. The flag list in proposal.md does not mention it. Apart from that, the gaps are flagged well: all 14 items and prices match the draft, and nothing is invented. But because so much data is missing, the printed menu is thin. No beer shows an ABV, no wine shows a region, the three spirits print with no description at all, and the Brut Rosé price has no glass or bottle label. The menu is not ready to publish until the venue answers the flags.
fixes: Put the draft's Manhattan public_components {"aromatic-bitters": false} back and remove 'aromatic bitters' from the printed description, or add it to the flags as a question for the venue: the draft hides the bitters but its own description names them.

Until brand and age data arrive, give each spirit a short type line built from the verified beverage_categories rows (for example 'Unaged blanco / plata tequila, served neat') rather than printing the name alone, and keep the brand/age flag open.

Mark the pending fields on the proof copy itself (for example greyed '[ABV]', '[region]' and '[glass/bottle]' next to the affected beer, wine and Brut Rosé lines), so a printed proof cannot pass as finished while the flags are open.

Close the empty space in El Barril by spacing the beer items like the other cards (or pairing it with a shorter card), and put doc.json's section order back to what prints (Cocktails, Beer, Cider, Wine, Spirits) so the phone and print versions don't disagree.
Style the spirits prices in the card accent colour like the other three cards, and move or shrink the Lotería card numbers (44 / 9 / 41 / 8) so guests can't mistake them for prices.

lens: Traced printed ingredients, garnishes, glass, serve and subhead labels to their sources (phg.menu_items plus phg.recipe_versions through current_recipe_version_id, project ddc4bb5b, gateway log_id 185), plus the Lotería card and Spanish usage
top_problem: All four cocktails trace cleanly to their recipe rows. The problem is the other 11 lines: beer, wine and spirits read like database classes ('Dry red wine.' for Malbec, 'Dry white wine.', 'Crisp pale lager.', 'Toasty amber lager.') or have no description at all (the three spirits). There is no grape, region, style detail or ABV, so half the menu lacks guest-language description.
verified: Margarita: rocks glass, lime wheel, 'Shake with ice and strain over fresh ice' (recipe_version f06abb74-762a-4f89-81b2-76a9e4714f3c). The words 'Bright and citrus-forward', blanco tequila, lime, orange liqueur and agave come from menu_items.menu_description. 'fresh lime' and 'agave syrup' trace to draft_doc component names (Fresh Lime Juice, Agave Syrup).
Manhattan: coupe and cocktail cherry (recipe_versions.glassware and garnish). Rye, sweet vermouth and aromatic bitters come from menu_description.

Brown Butter Old Fashioned: rocks glass and orange peel. 'Over a large cube' comes from the method 'Stir with ice and strain over a large cube'. Bourbon and demerara come from menu_description. Weak source: the draft says only 'bitters'; 'aromatic' comes from wording the Coordinator supplied (proposal line 114), not from a row.
House Daiquiri: coupe, lime coin, white rum, lime and house demerara syrup all match the recipe row and menu_description.
Beer, wine, cider and spirits descriptions match menu_items.menu_description word for word, and every price matches menu_price.
Lotería cards and verses are correct: El Cantarito 44, El Barril 9, La Rosa 41, La Botella 8, with their traditional verses and correct accents (cántaro, bebió, quedó, albañil).
problems: Crit 12: Malbec 'Dry red wine.', Pinot Grigio 'Dry white wine.' and the three beer lines are category wording, not guest language. The spirits print name only, with the card-level line 'Straight pours.'.
Crit 11/8: wines have no region, beers have no ABV, spirits have no brand or age. These are correctly flagged in missing_ingredients rather than invented, which is good, but the menu prints thin.

Crit 13: this is a Mexican cantina in Iowa City, yet it has no mezcal, no Mexican lager, only one agave cocktail (the Margarita) and a Cognac line. The Spanish kickers are used correctly, but the list does not read as a cantina. Junmai Ginjo (menu_items row, 12) is left off pending the venue's decision, which is correct.

Crit 14: the El Barril draft items sit about 135 px apart at preview scale, against about 75 px in La Rosa. The one-line beer descriptions float in large empty space, while the spirits card has no description measure at all. Spirits prices have no pour-size label (for example 2 oz).
fixes: Ask the venue for wine region and producer, beer brewery, style and ABV, and spirits brand and age. Until they arrive, rewrite the generic lines in guest language using only row facts (for example, Malbec: 'Dry, full red by the glass').
Designer: tighten or equalise the El Barril item spacing to match La Rosa, so each one-line description sits under its name instead of floating.
Add a pour-size label to La Botella once the venue supplies it. Until then, avoid implying a standard pour.
Flag to the Coordinator that the agave or Mexican beer offer is thin for a Mexican cantina (no mezcal, no Mexican lager). This is an item-list decision for the venue, not an edit to make.
Confirm 'aromatic' for the Old Fashioned bitters against a recipe_components row, or print 'bitters' as the draft does.

lens: description quality and one guest voice
top_problem: There are two voices on the menu. The four cocktails get real guest copy plus a serve line, and every serve and garnish traces to phg.recipe_versions: Margarita 14555870 is Rocks / Lime wheel, Manhattan bf732e78 is Coupe / Cocktail cherry, Brown Butter Old Fashioned 0cc4e912 is Rocks / Orange peel / large cube, and House Daiquiri 44dcba6e is Coupe / Lime coin. The other 10 items print catalogue labels that repeat or classify the name: 'Dry red wine.' (Malbec f6f9d57e), 'Dry white wine.' (Pinot Grigio 5ba7511f), 'Hop-forward draft IPA.' (8fb136cd), 'Toasty amber lager.' (70657e1e), 'Dry sparkling cider.' (65c39a14) and 'Dry sparkling rosé.' (32a35bd3). The three spirits (19d79518, 124f8949, 75501d63) have no description, only a shared 'Straight pours.' line. The Lotería card concept (El Cantarito 44, El Barril 9, La Rosa 41, La Botella 8, with the correct verses and accents) promises a storyteller's voice, and the copy under it reads like database classes.
fixes: Rewrite the 10 beer, wine, cider and spirit descriptions in the cocktail voice as short sensory lines that use only the facts in phg.menu_items.menu_description (for example Amber Lager 70657e1e: 'toasty' plus 'lager'). Never repeat the item name or a class word such as 'red wine' or 'IPA', and send missing_ingredients for grape region, beer ABV and tequila or cognac brand and age instead of padding.

Make the cocktail voice consistent. Only the Margarita opens with a tasting clause ('Bright and citrus-forward:'); either give each cocktail one sourced sensory lead or drop it. Also standardise the serve lines, which currently mix 'On the rocks,' 'In a coupe,' and 'Over a large cube,' into one pattern (glass, then garnish).

Layout note for the designer: the El Barril card has about 3 empty lines under each one-line beer description, so prices float away from their items. Tighten the spacing or use the space for longer copy.

Layout note for the designer: the description measure changes from item to item. Margarita and Old Fashioned break early ('blanco tequila, / fresh lime...') while House Daiquiri runs the full width. Set one measure per card so the lines break evenly.

Venue fit: add a short English gloss or tagline under each Spanish Lotería verse (or under the card name) so Iowa City guests who don't read Spanish get the joke, and consider noting tequila as the house emphasis in La Botella, since the Mexican-cantina identity currently rests on only the Margarita and two tequila pours.

lens: Venue-type fit: Mexican cantina and cocktail bar in Iowa City (ZCTA 52240); Spanish and lotería usage including verses
top_problem: The lotería layer is accurate and ownable, but everything under it reads like a generic American bar. Of 13 printed drinks, the Margarita is the only agave cocktail. Wine and beer descriptions are category labels ('Dry red wine.', 'Dry white wine.', 'Hop-forward draft IPA.'). The three spirits print with no description at all. The masthead 'Cantina & Cocktail Bar / IOWA CITY, IOWA' could belong to any venue. The Spanish is chrome on the headers and never reaches the guest-facing copy.
verified: Lotería numbers and verses match the Don Clemente deck: 44 El Cantarito 'Tanto va el cántaro al agua, que se quiebra y te moja las enaguas'; 9 El Barril 'Tanto bebió el albañil, que quedó como barril'; 41 La Rosa 'Rosita, Rosaura, ven que te quiero ahora'; 8 La Botella 'La herramienta del borracho'. Accents are correct (cántaro, bebió, quedó).

Serve cues trace to phg.recipe_versions via menu_items.current_recipe_version_id: Margarita glassware Rocks, garnish Lime wheel (printed 'On the rocks, lime wheel'); Manhattan Coupe, Cocktail cherry; Brown Butter Old Fashioned Rocks, Orange peel, method 'strain over a large cube'; House Daiquiri Coupe, Lime coin. All match.

Descriptions trace to phg.menu_items.menu_description: Margarita 'Tequila blanco, lime, orange liqueur, agave. Bright and citrus-forward.'; Manhattan 'Rye, sweet vermouth, aromatic bitters.'; Old Fashioned 'Brown butter-washed bourbon, demerara, bitters.'; Daiquiri 'White rum, lime, and house demerara syrup.'; beer, wine and cider text is printed verbatim from menu_description.

Census phg_census_zcta 52240 (ACS 2020-2024): median age 28.6, 21-34 share 29.9%, Hispanic/Latino 11%, median household income $52,960, $100k+ households 26.1%, bachelor's or higher 47.6%. This is a young college-town crowd, so cocktails at $14-16 sit at the top of the local price tier.
problems: Criterion 11: 'fresh lime' on the Margarita and the Daiquiri, 'agave syrup' and 'aromatic bitters' on the Old Fashioned are wording the designer added. The source rows say 'lime', 'agave' and 'bitters'. These are small, but they are not what the source says.
Criterion 11 and coherence: the draft has 15 menu_items, including Junmai Ginjo ('Junmai Ginjo sake.'), which does not appear on the printed tabla and is not accounted for in the proposal.

Criterion 12: the beer, wine and cider lines are category labels. 'Dry red wine.' on a Malbec and 'Hop-forward draft IPA.' on the IPA mostly repeat the name. The spirits print price only, and the card-level 'Straight pours.' does not give a guest any reason to order.

Criterion 13: the Spanish/English subhead pairs are inconsistent. CLÁSICOS, DE LA CASA, SIDRA and ESPUMOSO are Spanish glossed in English, but 'AGAVE · Tequila' and 'BRANDY · Cognac' are not translations.
